what: 50-step gate of a null Numba plugin bound in shadow at the compute_uwshcu_inv hook (the original answers; the plugin's cost is timed), on the first image carrying the batch-A hooks
job: validation/jobs/pi_cam_pausable_50step.pbs (derived script with export lines; 4 nodes x 64 GB requested)
bfb_record_note: the bfb file written by the job compares one candidate file against four and says false; the run never reached its restart, so the comparison is void
outcome: killed at the memory limit during step 1, when every rank compiled the plugin (forrtl error 78, process killed; two ranks also hit an LLVM assertion in Value::getValueName)
diagnosis: the base run uses about 230 GB of the 256 GB requested (4 x 64 GB); the Numba compile of a plugin with 57 arguments peaks near 260 MB a process on the login node, about 30 GB more a node at 128 ranks, which crossed the limit.  Not a hook fault: the nothing-armed and everything gates on the same image are bit-for-bit.
disposition: rerun with 200 GB requested a node (the nodes have 240 GB); a compile once a node, shared through the Numba cache, is the durable fix if the larger request is not enough
